cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Still a Good Sign
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You've postponed dinner again. You still hate disappointing me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the third time. I feel awful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. After three cancellations, my feelings still matter to you. That means something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop holding Fridays for me. I can't promise anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're protecting my Fridays now. I'll leave the date open; we're already looking after each other.

mechanism: A credits repeated cancellation as the pupil learning consideration, converting reduced contact into proof they still care for each other.
confusable: Not merely forgiving cancellation: A treats its disappointment as ongoing influence and attachment.
comparison: Direct unwanted company versus relinquished calendar commitment.
